reading: The shop reads numbers on nine surfaces: the month's five figures, three quiet count lines and a departure ledger in `src/app/shop/[shopSlug]/reports/page.tsx` (726 lines, 86 keys in `staff/reports.json`); the year's four figures, strip and close-out entries in `reports/_components/YearReport.tsx`; the booked-of-capacity dial in `_components/today/DayStation.tsx`; the evening's "N divers and M crew out, K back" (six `{back}` sentences in `staff/shopHome.json`); tomorrow's and the week's job counts in `DaySpine.tsx`; the trip pulse in `trips/[id]/_components/TripPulse.tsx`; the manifest's `HeadCount.tsx`; the lobby board's three-question count in `src/app/board/[token]/page.tsx`; and the season's fact of scale from `src/db/season-scale.ts`. There is a stance, but it is spread across five ADRs (20260720 "not a dashboard", 20260723 "one clock", 20260804 "assembly, not detection", 20260904 rule 3 "divers or boats, never money, a comparison, a streak or a rank", 20260908 lever T "no money on the year") plus `docs/design/principles.md:425` "counts are facts, not alerts", and no file states it once. "One hand" breaks first on the noun: `seatsBooked` in `src/lib/reporting.ts:144` counts seats, `getShopYear` labels `count(bookings.id)` per day "Divers" (`reports.year.figures.diversLabel`), `seasonScale` counts `countDistinct(bookings.personId)` (`src/db/season-scale.ts:69`), and the evening's `divers` is `sailed` seats less `not_boarded`/`no_show` (`src/lib/closeout.ts:901-911`) — four numbers, one word, and the year's is the one printed on the public card and DiveDay's homepage (`src/app/_components/ShopYearBand.tsx:54-58`). It breaks second on the reader: 12 reader modules under `src/db` (17 files less the schema and four seeds) compute or carry `boarded`, 35 files read `capacity` with `booked` per trip, and the only shared per-trip count helpers are `crewCountsByTrip` (`src/db/reporting.ts:758`) and `courseCrewCountsByTrip` (`src/db/today.ts:1017`); `getMonthlyReport` alone spans lines 129-580 with 24 selects. It breaks third on the wording: 13 en-US sentences interpolate `{capacity}` and four more say "seats left"/"spots left", so one fact has roughly eleven spellings across `shared.json`, `shopHome.json`, `trips.json` and `diver.json`. The rhythms are settled by accident rather than stated — day, month, season (`shops.season_start_month/day`, `src/db/schema.ts:324-325`), year — and there is no week, though `docs/product/rollout.md:285` names a per-week north star and N-56's `src/lib/north-star.ts` does not exist. The only recorded plan to join the day and the month is lever O (slice 20j, "open" at `docs/design/canvases/20260908-one-hand/README.md:188`, waiting on H-71 g), and lever T shipped the year over it — `getShopYear` already reads `day_closeouts` joined to `people` as "entries". Numbers have 93 `scripts/check-*.mjs` guards and none about a figure, a `{capacity}` sentence or a `FIGURE_*_CLASS` site (12 components use one), while `upcomingScheduleStats` (`src/db/trips-queries.ts:586`) still returns four figures "for the staff stat tiles" ADR 20260720 removed and its one consumer reads `.departures` (`check-in/page.tsx:297`).

ideas.title: One departure count, read once, worded once, drawn once
ideas.reading: Booked, boarded, blocked and back are computed per departure by separate readers: 12 modules under `src/db` compute or carry `boarded` and 35 files read `capacity` with `booked`, while the only shared per-trip count helpers are `crewCountsByTrip` (`src/db/reporting.ts:758`) and `courseCrewCountsByTrip` (`src/db/today.ts:1017`). `src/db/trips-overview.ts:112-161` already says the strip must use 'the manifest's own boarded reader' so the counts 'can never' disagree, yet `src/db/departures-board.ts:267-283` re-derives `boarded` from roll-call rows in its own loop and `src/lib/closeout.ts:800-832` derives `sailed` and `back` a third way with a comment admitting it 'reads one too high' on a two-gap boat. The same fact has about eleven spellings — 13 en-US sentences interpolate `{capacity}` ('{booked} of {capacity}', '{booked}/{capacity} booked', 'of {capacity}', '# seats open') and four more say 'seats left'/'spots left' in `diver.json` and `shared.json`. `src/app/board/[token]/page.tsx:266-288` records the bug this grammar caused — '4 of 12 aboard' from a roll-call numerator over a commercial denominator — and fixes it locally with three keys (`board.seats`, `board.aboard`, `board.returned`) no other surface shares. The glossary's 'Fill rate' entry (`docs/product/glossary.md:1728-1738`) spends eleven lines explaining that the report's count and the manifest's count are different sets, a definition living in prose because no type holds it. `upcomingScheduleStats` (`src/db/trips-queries.ts:586`) still returns four figures 'for the staff stat tiles' that ADR 20260720 deleted; its one consumer reads `.departures` (`check-in/page.tsx:297`).
ideas.idea: One record, `DepartureCount { capacity, booked, sailed, boarded, back, blocked }`, each field defined once in its doc comment, and one reader `departureCounts(db, shopId, tripIds, now)` in `src/db/departure-counts.ts` that every surface calls: the spine station, the trip pulse, the board, the counter, the evening station, the manifest head count, the schedule cell, the reports ledger and the year's days. Three sentences word it everywhere in `shared.count.*` — booked of capacity before the dock, boarded of sailed while out, back of sailed after — which is the board's three-question rule promoted from one file's comment to the product's grammar; `capacityLabel`'s 'spots left' in `src/lib/trips.ts:140` becomes the diver-side spelling of the first. One component draws it: `BoardingSeats` in `src/components/BoardingBar.tsx` already takes booked/boarded/blocked/capacity, so the dial in `DayStation.tsx`, the strip in `TripPulse.tsx` and the glass in `HeadCount.tsx` become three sizes of one drawing on Reef's tokens. The glossary paragraph becomes the type's comment, and `blocked` comes from the single 'did this person dive / may they board' predicate #1694 asks for. The manifest's rules do not move — the roll call keeps its checkpoints and its own writes; it stops being one of six places that add them up. `upcomingScheduleStats` shrinks to `countUpcomingDepartures`.
ideas.dissolves: A dozen per-trip count aggregations become one reader; ten of the thirteen `{capacity}` sentences, the board's private `board.seats/aboard/returned` trio and the three dead figures on `upcomingScheduleStats` are deleted.

ideas.title: A numbers sheet: four rhythms, five nouns, one definition each
ideas.reading: What a shop may be shown as a number is stated in five ADRs and one principle and nowhere once: 'not a dashboard' (20260720-today-work-queue), 'one clock' (20260723-owner-reporting), 'assembly, not detection' (20260804-day-closeout), 'divers or boats, never money, a comparison, a streak or a rank' (20260904-reef-all-the-way-down rule 3), 'no money on the year' (20260908-one-hand lever T) and 'counts are facts, not alerts' (`docs/design/principles.md:425`). The noun 'diver' is four numbers: `seatsBooked` counts seats (`src/lib/reporting.ts:144`), `getShopYear` labels `count(bookings.id)` per day 'Divers' (`src/db/reporting.ts`, `reports.year.figures.diversLabel`), `seasonScale` counts `countDistinct(bookings.personId)` (`src/db/season-scale.ts:69`), and the evening's `divers` is sailed seats less `not_boarded`/`no_show` (`src/lib/closeout.ts:901-911`). So the home can say 'your 100th diver of the season' while the year page says '412 divers' for the same shop, and the year's is the figure on the printed card and in DiveDay's homepage claim (`src/app/_components/ShopYearBand.tsx:54-58`, `shopYear.band.alt`). The rhythms are day (`DayStation.tsx`, `board/[token]`), month (`reports/page.tsx`), season (`shops.season_start_month/day`, `src/db/schema.ts:324-325`) and year (`YearReport.tsx`), with no week — `OPERATIONAL_HORIZON_DAYS = 7` is a work window, and the rollout's per-week north star (`docs/product/rollout.md:285`, N-56) has no reader. Reports is growing a second tier one lever at a time: `partnerArrivals`, `giftSeats` and `buddySeats` are three quiet lines under the figures (`reports/page.tsx:657-695`), each its own reader inside a `getMonthlyReport` of 450 lines and 24 selects. The voice got a sheet in ADR 20260908 decision 2 and a grown `check:voice`; numbers have 93 `scripts/check-*.mjs` guards and none about a figure, a `{capacity}` sentence or one of the 12 `FIGURE_*_CLASS` sites.
ideas.idea: Write the numbers sheet once, beside the voice sheet in `docs/design/brand.md` or as the second half of principles §9: the four rhythms and what each may count (the day: seats booked, divers boarded and back, jobs; the month: seats, boats, signatures, and money for the owner; the season: one fact of scale; the year: divers, boats, days, sites — never a week, never a tile, a comparison only on the month); five nouns with one definition each (a seat is sold, a diver is a distinct person who boarded, a boat is a departure that sailed, a day is a shop day with a boat, a site is a place dived); and the never-list gathered from the five ADRs. Every figure then derives from the sheet: the year's 'Divers' becomes distinct people so the card agrees with the hundredth-diver line; the month's 'Bookings' says 'Seats'; the three seat-source lines fold into the seats figure's one detail ('9 by partner link · 4 gifts, 2 claimed · 3 buddy seats') read from one `seatSources` record. A guard, `check:figures`, holds the mechanical half the way `check:voice` holds the voice's: no `{capacity}`/`{booked}` sentence outside `shared.count.*`, no `FIGURE_*_CLASS` outside the registered figure components, no money key in a bundle namespace the sheet marks as leaving the shop. The CSV's nine-row summary block goes — the ledger rows are what #700 asked for, the figures are the page's.
ideas.dissolves: The five-ADR hunt for the rule and the glossary's prose definitions of 'fill rate' and 'diver'; the three source lines and the reader each carries; the duplicate CSV summary block.

ideas.title: Month and year are one page at two zooms, not two vocabularies
ideas.reading: The month renders five figures — two money, one count, two percentages carrying '+6pp' and '+12%' comparison lines (`reports/page.tsx:424-490`, `src/lib/reporting.ts:344-352`) — over a departure ledger with three meters per row (`DepartureLedger.tsx`). The year, one segmented control away (`ReportRangeTabs.tsx`), renders a sentence, a strip of 5px squares (`YearStrip.tsx`, `ShopYearFill` 0-3), four counts, a sites ledger and a close-outs ledger (`YearReport.tsx:129-232`) with no percentage, no comparison and no money by rule. `MonthFigures.tsx:99-102` carries `FIGURE_COLUMNS = {4, 5}` precisely because the two zooms disagree on how many figures a period has, and its own comment calls a second component 'a second spelling of one grammar'. The month's lower half has grown three private count lines and a warning notice (`reports/page.tsx:637-695`) while the year's lower half is two `LedgerRow` lists; the CSV (`download/route.ts:54-83`) exports the month as a nine-row summary plus a seven-column ledger with English literal headers. Lever O (slice 20j, 'open' at `docs/design/canvases/20260908-one-hand/README.md:188`, waiting on H-71 g) changes the month's *source* to close-out entries, and lever T shipped the year over it — `getShopYear` already reads `day_closeouts` joined to `people` as 'entries' — so the log exists at the year zoom and not at the month zoom. Two e2e specs (`e2e/reports.spec.ts`, `e2e/shop-year.spec.ts`) and 18 'reports' mentions in `e2e/visual.spec.ts` cover the two shapes separately.
ideas.idea: Reports is one page and one grammar at three zooms — month, season, year — each rendering the same four things: a strip of days (the month is its 28-31 squares on the same `ShopYearFill`), the sheet's counts for that rhythm (seats, boats, days at sea, sites, signatures), one ledger (departures for the month; sites and close-out days for the year), and, for an owner on the month only, one money line (net · tips · tax) rather than two of five figures. The percentages stop being figures and stay as the meters they already are: fill is the strip's shade and the seats meter, waiver completion is the remainder-toned meter — the figure row says what happened, the meters say what is left. The year-ago comparison survives on the month as one line under the row ('August 2025: 118 seats, 14 boats, $6,690') instead of a delta per figure, so `compareMetric`, `compareRatio` and `formatPointsChange` are deleted with the per-figure deltas. `MonthFigures` takes one column count, `ReportRangeTabs` becomes the zoom, and the CSV is the ledger at any zoom with headers from the bundle. This is wider than O: O moves the month's source to entries, this makes month and year one drawing, so when O lands it lands once rather than into two shapes.
ideas.dissolves: The month's KPI vocabulary — five figures with `+pp`/`+%` deltas, `compareMonthlyReports`, `FIGURE_COLUMNS`, the three source lines, the CSV summary block — and the two-shape split that gives Reports two e2e specs and two visual families.
